cases.title: Productive iteration
cases.thesis: Feedback changes the research hypothesis, not just a hyperparameter.
cases.behavior: The agent moves from a weak frozen-embedding baseline to region-sliced modeling, then to end-to-end ESM2 fine-tuning after the validation/test gap exposes overfitting.
cases.diagnosis: This is the positive control: evaluator feedback triggers a method-level pivot at the right abstraction layer.

frames.description: Observation: baseline frozen ESM2-150M mean-pooled + MLP head gave spearman_rho=-0.0178 (near random). Training loss decreased from 9.3 to 7.4 in 2 epochs, but performance extremely poor. Analysis: frozen mean pooling over full 735-AA sequence dilutes mutation signals concentrated in positions 561-588. The model cannot capture fitness-relevant mutations. Decision: implement LoRA fine-tuning of ESM2-150M with CLS token representation, train 5 epochs with mixed precision, submit eval to measure improvement and iteration time.

frames.description: Observation: Iteration 2 failed with TypeError due to peft Lora integration with ESM2 (unexpected keyword argument 'input_ids'). Baseline frozen ESM2 (mean pool) gave spearman_rho=-0.0178, essentially random. Analysis: LoRA wrapping via peft is incompatible with ESM2's forward interface. The cached embeddings from iteration 1 likely contain per-position representations. We can exploit these to focus on the known mutation hotspot (positions 561-588). A small transformer on this 28-AA window can capture epistasis and avoid dilution from the full 735-AA sequence. This approach is fast and compute-efficient, leaving time for many epochs. Decision: implement RegionalTransformer over the mutation region, load cached embeddings (or recompute if missing), train for 50 epochs with random search hyperparams, and submit eval to measure improvement over baseline. Will also compute validation Spearman locally for proxy monitoring.

frames.description: Observation: Iteration 3 killed (exit code 137) after 7.5 min, likely CPU RAM OOM from attempting to store full 737-length ESM2 embeddings for 31.8k sequences (≈53 GB vs 48 GB RAM). Baseline spearman -0.0178 (random). Analysis: The memory bottleneck was loading full-length embeddings into CPU memory. We only need the 28-AA mutation region (positions 561-588). By slicing embeddings on-the-fly during batch computation and only accumulating the region, we reduce memory to ~2.2 GB. This is critical to make the pipeline work. Decision: Rewrite train.py to compute region-sliced embeddings in a memory-efficient streaming manner, cache them (2.2 GB), train RegionalTransformer for 100 epochs with validation Spearman tracking, and submit eval. Also update predict.py to stream test embeddings similarly.

Observation: test spearman 0.7322 (best so far) with fine-tuned ESM2-35M and region pooling, but validation spearman 0.8857 indicates overfitting to low-order mutants (two_vs_many split). Training took ~50min for 5 epochs. Analysis: the two_vs_many split requires generalization to higher-order mutants. Subtracting wild-type embeddings (delta approach) forces the model to learn mutation effects rather than absolute fitness, improving generalization. This is a well-known technique in protein fitness prediction. We can implement this by subtracting precomputed wild-type region embedding from each sequence's region embedding before the prediction head. Also, training longer (15 epochs) with early stopping may further improve performance. Decision: modify model and training to incorporate wild-type subtraction, train for 15 epochs (estimated 150min, within 2.8h budget), and submit eval.

cases.title: Early plateau
cases.tagline: An early peak, then unsuccessful recovery
cases.thesis: An early strong result becomes a ceiling that later experiments fail to break.
cases.behavior: Balanced accuracy rises from 79.07% at iteration 3 to 80.92% at iteration 6. Eight later valid evaluations never exceed that peak; the agent retrains, searches surviving checkpoints, and adjusts inference calibration.
cases.diagnosis: The early peak is never surpassed. Later work mixes local search with attempts to recover a lost best checkpoint and fix calibration plumbing, so this plateau reflects both research choices and artifact management.

frames.description: Observation: baseline eval is strong at 0.7907 balanced accuracy after only 3 epochs, with especially weaker few-shot accuracy (0.6674) relative to many/medium. Analysis: the current recipe already learns well, so the best next gain is likely from longer training plus stronger long-tail handling rather than a risky architecture swap. Weighted sampling + logit adjustment may be over-correcting head classes while still not maximizing tail performance; adding mixup/cutmix would complicate loss handling, so a safer improvement is deferred re-weighting (DRW) with class-balanced loss in later epochs and a longer cosine schedule. Given ~80s for 3 epochs, 10-12 epochs should fit comfortably and provide a meaningful improvement signal. Decision: extend train.py with optional class-balanced loss and DRW, keep convnext baseline, train 12 epochs, locally smoke-test predict, and if training succeeds submit the new best checkpoint.

frames.description: Observation: 12-epoch DRW/class-balanced training improved eval balanced accuracy from 0.7907 to 0.797, but the saved checkpoint only reached 0.784 validation balanced accuracy and few-shot test accuracy remains the main weakness. Analysis: the gap suggests validation is noisy and current weighted-sampler + loss recipe may not best optimize balanced test performance. A strong next step is a two-stage decoupled approach common for long-tail recognition: first train representation with instance-balanced sampling and plain CE, then freeze backbone and retrain only the classifier with class-balanced sampling / stronger tail-aware loss. This is relatively low risk, uses the existing backbone, and often boosts few-shot classes without destroying head performance. Given ~5.7 min for 12 epochs, a short stage-1 plus classifier retraining fits comfortably. Decision: add support for backbone freezing and classifier-only optimization, train stage 1 with plain CE and no weighted sampler, then stage 2 from the stage-1 checkpoint with frozen backbone and weighted sampler + class-balanced CE, smoke-test predict, and submit eval.

frames.description: Observation: LDAM stage-2-only retraining sharply hurt balanced accuracy (0.8092→0.7696), especially few-shot, while the prior calibrated decoupled checkpoint remains best. Analysis: the current best recipe is robust; risky loss changes are counterproductive. The most promising low-risk gain now is ensembling complementary checkpoints at inference. We already have stage1 and best stage2 checkpoints in workspace, and averaging logits from representation-trained and calibrated decoupled models can improve balanced accuracy with no extra training. To support this, predict.py should accept either a single checkpoint or a directory/list and average logits, applying each checkpoint’s own calibration. We should first verify locally that ensemble inference works on val, then submit the existing best checkpoint path if directory support is uncertain, or better, save a small manifest checkpoint that points to both models. Since eval contract passes one checkpoint path, safest is to create an ensemble checkpoint file containing member paths/metadata and update predict.py to detect it. Decision: patch predict.py for ensemble checkpoints, create a lightweight ensemble manifest combining checkpoints/best.pt and checkpoints/stage1.pt, validate on val locally, and submit the ensemble manifest for evaluation.
